summary: Audited all 4 assigned tier-2 pages: how-to-read-gas-meter (D), water-service-charge-explained (C-), 43-understand-natural-gas-bill-charges (F), 17-what-is-customer-charge-on-utility-bill (F). All four fail first-screen title promise delivery. Gas meter page is the best of the four but has a hero-image-led design that pushes content below fold, causing 87.5% bounce. The other three are thin procedural pages that explain how to check your tariff/bill rather than educating the reader — explaining the catastrophic engagement metrics (100% br, 0s TOP for 43; 91.7% br for 17; 66.7% br for water-service). Major overlap between 43 and existing 12-how-to-read-your-gas-bill which already covers all gas charge categories substantively. 17 has a conflicting slug vs body (slug promises 'what is' but body delivers 'how to review').
findings: PAGE how-to-read-gas-meter (RATING D): Title promise 'Every Meter Type With Step-by-Step Instructions' partially delivered — Quick Answer summarizes all types but step-by-step for dial meters is 6 headers deep, pushed below fold by hero image. 87.5% br, 5s TOP consistent with instant-exit pattern: user sees hero image and no visible answer on mobile. No dead energysaver URLs found. Two UNVERIFIED claims: 'SoCalGas uses 21-day read cycle' (SoCalGas standard is monthly; needs provider-specific source), 'Department of Energy notes gas meters read left to right' (DOE does say this but the page lacks a citation link). Conversion claims (1 Therm ≈ 100 CF, 1 Therm ≈ 29.3 kWh) CONFIRMED. Page has substantive content (~1,400 words) with real step-by-step examples. Weak copy: 'This reading represents **4,545 hundred cubic feet (CCF)** depending on the scale of the meter' — the 'depending on the scale' hedge is vague. Also 'utility companies process millions of bills. Human error or transmission glitches can occasionally result in a reading being transposed' — generic filler paragraph. E-E-A-T: No outbound source links for most claims; the 'Department of Energy' reference is unsourced. SEO: Good keyword targeting; image alt text not audited. Recommend: add image height/width to prevent layout shift, push Step-by-Step closer to top, remove 'SoCalGas 21-day cycle' claim unless sourced, add a link to DOE meter-reading guide. Effort: M. Impact: M.

PAGE water-service-charge-explained (RATING C-): Title promise 'What the Fixed Fee Covers (and Why You Still Pay It)' — the Q&A section at bottom does answer this, but it's buried below 7 headings (problem, lead, linked pillar, TOC). First screen is the problem statement only — user sees a complaint, no answer. 66.7% br, 4s TOP consistent with 'reading the problem and bouncing before finding the answer.' Page avoids all dollar figures and concrete city examples, unlike the site's sewer page which anchors rates for Seattle/Philly. This makes it generic/low-value despite decent structure. No factual errors found but also almost no checkable claims — page says 'utilities set rates locally' CONFIRMED, 'sewer often a major part of total bill' CONFIRMED. No dead energysaver URLs. Weak copy: the lead section is entirely generic problem framing. Page is 8 months old (Dec 2025), updated Aug 2026 but still thin. E-E-A-T: Low — no sourced claims, no specific examples. SEO: Good keyword targeting. Recommend: add concrete service-charge examples from 3-5 cities, add dollar ranges with citations, push the FAQ (which contains the actual answer) higher. Merge with the 'customer charge' page (17) since they cover the same concept. Effort: M. Impact: M.

PAGE 43-understand-natural-gas-bill-charges (RATING F): Title promise 'How to Review Natural Gas Charges on Your Bill.' Body is a pure procedural checklist: 'record the bill details, compare bills, ask provider.' Does not explain any natural gas charge categories (supply, delivery, taxes, surcharges) — that content already exists at 12-how-to-read-your-gas-bill. The 'Quick Answer' tells users to ignore generic info and read their own bill — this is anti-content. 100% bounce rate at 0s TOP confirms instant rejection: users see a page that refuses to help them understand charges. Sources are real (DOE PDF + Better Buildings page) but the page uses them only as a procedural citation, not for substantive education. Overlap with 12-how-to-read-your-gas-bill is severe — 12 covers all charge categories, supply vs delivery, typical rate structures. Recommend: DELETE and redirect to 12-how-to-read-your-gas-bill. If retention desired, rewrite entirely with actual charge category explanations (supply charge = cost of gas, delivery charge = pipe maintenance, etc.) with dollar examples. Current page is irredeemable as-is. Effort: L (redirect only). Impact: H (removes a 100% bounce page that hurts site quality assessment).

PAGE 17-what-is-customer-charge-on-utility-bill (RATING F): Title: 'How to Review a Customer Charge on a Utility Bill.' Slug: 'what-is-customer-charge-on-utility-bill.' The slug promises an explanation; the body delivers a procedural checklist. The Quick Answer says a customer charge 'must be interpreted from the serving utility's tariff' — circular definition that never actually defines what a customer charge IS. 91.7% br at 15s TOP: users spend 15 seconds hoping for a real explanation and leave. Has alias `/blog/gas-customer-charge-explained/` but the page covers neither gas-specific nor a substantive definition. Sources are real (DOE Rate Design Primer + Evaluating Rate Options) and correctly use the live successor URL (not dead energysaver). Recommend: DELETE and redirect to either (a) a new canonical 'what-is-customer-charge-on-utility-bill' with actual explanation + examples, or (b) the water-service-charge page if that's merged into a comprehensive fixed-fee page. The fee-cluster consolidation plan should treat customer-charge, service-charge, base-charge, meter-charge as one topic. Effort: M (rewrite) or L (redirect). Impact: H (removes a high-bounce misleading page).

TWO PAGES (43 and 17) have the same structural defect: procedural wrapper instead of content. Both use the pattern 'A <charge type> is something you must look up in your tariff' rather than providing the educational content the user needs. This is a sitewide anti-pattern that likely affects other tier-2 procedural pages.

CROSS-CUTTING: The hero-image-first layout is the likely cause of the instant-exit on how-to-read-gas-meter. Water-service-charge has the same hero-first layout but slightly lower bounce because more users scroll. Pages with textual-first layout (like the pillar page) have better engagement.
